rationale_overall: This week's pool surfaced one genuine catalyst worth flagging for future weeks — Amazon reportedly in talks to acquire Globalstar (GSAT) for ~$9B (moneycontrol 2026-04-02, corroborated by Yahoo Finance 2026-04-03 framing it as an Apple-satellite-partner risk) — a real M&A-driven satellite/space-infrastructure story adjacent to the rockets & spacecraft wave. However, none of the four managed holdings (GOOGL, NVDA, RKLB, SMR) showed a thesis-breach or peak-exhaustion signal this week to justify the paired removal a GSAT add would require: RKLB already anchors the rockets/spacecraft bucket with no negative news, NVDA/GOOGL got only reinforcing commentary (Huang's robotics remark; Pixel 10a review), and the SMR-adjacent nuclear item was a low-quality PR-wire 'market boom' press release, not a dated catalyst. Filtered as noise/non-investable: private-company launches (SpaceX, ULA joint venture, Starlink breakup), foreign-government programs (Artemis II/NASA, Russia's Plesetsk military satellite, ISRO Mission MITRA, Saudi Shams satellite, India's Suryastra rocket system), pure geopolitical/conflict reporting with no listed-equity angle (Iran/Israel/Kuwait missile and drone exchanges, Ukraine war updates, Kim Jong Un missile test, F-35 crash/losses), keyword false-matches (Rocket Pharmaceuticals/RCKT is gene-therapy biotech not spaceflight; 'Rocket Close/Better' in Scotsman Guide is Rocket Mortgage/RKT, not aerospace), thinly-traded/foreign-exchange tickers (NXN.V on the CVE), pre-IPO private raises (Rebellions AI chip startup), and generic AI-hype op-eds/policy pieces with no specific ticker. Pratt & Whitney's $3.8B F135 deal (RTX) and Lockheed's missile-margin story (LMT) are noted as candidate defense/geopolitical exposure for a future rebalance but do not clear the bar alone without a paired removal this week. Holding steady.
